points.description: States that an SVM finds a decision boundary (separating hyperplane) that classifies the data into classes with maximum margin, i.e. the boundary is placed to maximise the gap between the classes. Equivalent wording such as 'hyperplane that maximises the margin' earns the mark. Saying only 'it classifies data' without the maximum-margin idea does not earn it.

States that the support vectors are the data points nearest the decision boundary and that the margin is determined by these points. Equivalent wording earns the mark. Kernels, quadratic programming and 'linear learnable machines' are correct but are not required for full marks.

rubric.notes: Full marks for a student who gives the maximum-margin decision boundary and the support vectors near it, in any equivalent wording. Half-credit is not used because each point is all-or-nothing. A student who gives only one of the two ideas gets 1 mark, and a vague answer with neither gets 0. Kernels and quadratic programming are correct model-answer content but are secondary for a 2-mark question, so they are not required.
